verdict: A tidy, fully in-band Fire Joker-style 3×3 classic in arcade costume that players understand easily, but its theme and mechanism don't need each other and the bonus is just base spins with a bigger multiplier, so it is competent and forgettable.
pros: Every measured band is in, RTP is exact at 96.00%, and the declared medium volatility matches the measured SD of 7.6.
Very readable for a player: the panel player understood the top pay, the trigger, the wild and the feature correctly, and the win labels ('Marquee ×3 · +4.98') make each payout checkable.
The pixel lows are distinct by colour and shape at size, and the Glitch block wild and Golden token scatter stand out from the paying symbols.
cons: Give the feature an arcade action instead of a richer multiplier table: e.g. a 'Hi-Score' meter that banks each free-spin win and raises the Marquee floor one step per paying spin, or 'extra life' retriggers, so the bonus is the theme's climax rather than base spins with a bigger number.
Redraw the Neon seven as the loudest icon on the board (larger multicolour seven-segment digit with a glow and a gold plate) so the 83× premium reads above the rocket at a glance.
Only animate or light the Marquee on spins with a line win (or grey it out on dead spins): today ×10 and ×25 light up on losing spins, which reads as a win and then deflates.

Move the Bonus stage start card off the grid (or below it) and hold the triggering board for a beat in Turbo too, so all three Golden tokens are seen before 'Free spin 1 of 10'; make the BIG WIN panel opaque and hold it until dismissed.
confusions: The natural bonus in Turbo started without my seeing the trigger board or the Start card; the screen just jumped to 'Bonus stage, Free spin 1 of 10', with only two tokens visible.
On the forced trigger, the start card covered the middle cell, so only two of the three golden tokens were visible.
The paytable says 'Match 3 on a line' but heart pairs pay 0.25× (two hearts listed separately); a heart + glitch pair also paid as 2 hearts.
